newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude grades find support from late API data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude grades find support from late API data.

text.p: U.S. grades were easier late Tuesday but found support from larger-than-expected draws in total crude stocks, and a hefty deficit in the Gulf Coast.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) inventory report showed overall stocks fell 3.3 million barrels for the week of September 6, with PADD 3 stocks down 5.5 million barrels.
Differentials held at weaker intraday levels, partly due to the narrower Oct/Nov West Texas Intermediate spread.
October WTI/Cushing was at $24.10-24.20 a barrel, 40 cents over Monday's cash market, with the Oct/Nov spread unchanged at 62 cents, down from 70 cents earlier.
U.S. crude runs were up at 94.7 percent, compared with 94.4 percent the previous week, signalling good refiner demand alongside a need to restock on low product inventories.
"Going into the winter with such low heating oil stocks could be a lot of trouble. I don't see demand tailing off," a Midwest trader said, noting a drop in North Sea cargoes.
The Atlantic arbitrage has shut for now, although weaker Dated Brent could soon pry open the import window again.
In the domestic market, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James traded from plus 38 to 34 cents, down three cents, with WTI at Midland at plus 6-8 cents, also down three cents.
West Texas Intermediate/Cushing Posting Plus changed hands early at postings plus $2.29, but rebounded to $2.38/39 late as the Oct/Nov WTI spread relaxed.
Sour grades remained largely unchanged in moderate action undaunted by the availability of regional sours.
West Texas Sour/Midland moved at minus $1.18/1.19, and Eugene Island at minus $1.05, unchanged from previously.
